about: sedi-1's verifier cases: each fixture is a bundle in the form acdc_build reads, and each case names the sedi-1 choices its verdict rests on and its security triage, and lists every finding the sedi-1 model makes. The verdict itself is the model's (generators/spec_tables/sedi_cases.py).

cases.title: Issued under the event seal
cases.description: A credential issued to its holder in a blindable registry of its own, each registry event anchored in the issuer's KEL by the event seal {i, s, d} whose i is the registry's SAID. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Issued under the seal couple
cases.description: As SV-01, with every registry event anchored by the couple {s, d}. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Update anchored by a bare digest
cases.description: As SV-01, but the registry update that issues the credential is anchored only by a bare digest {d}, which sedi-1 does not accept as a seal. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a registry event whose anchor the profile refuses.

cases.title: Event seal naming the issuer, not the registry
cases.description: As SV-01, but the update's event seal names the issuer's prefix in i rather than the registry's SAID. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a seal that names the wrong log.

cases.title: Seal couple with an extra field
cases.description: As SV-02, but the update's seal carries a field beyond s and d. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a seal of a shape the profile refuses.

cases.title: Revoked
cases.description: The credential's registry head records it revoked. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a revoked credential.

cases.title: Update withheld before a revocation
cases.description: The credential is issued at n=1 and revoked at n=3; the bundle withholds the event at n=2. The verifier cannot account for the registry past n=1. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete, never valid at the earlier head.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets a holder hide a revocation by withholding the event before it.

cases.title: Head update undisclosed
cases.description: The credential is issued at n=1 and the registry has an anchored update at n=2 whose blinded state the bundle does not disclose. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts an issued state the registry may since have changed.

cases.title: Two updates anchored at one sequence number
cases.description: Two different registry updates both claim n=1, and the issuer's KEL anchors both. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets either of two duplicitous states stand.

cases.title: One-hop chain under I2I
cases.description: N, issued by I to H, has one edge with the I2I operator to F, issued by Q to I. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Edge with no operator
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge names no operator; the default for a targeted far node is I2I, which holds. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Edge with no operator, default fails
cases.description: As SV-11, but F is issued to R, so the default I2I does not hold. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a chain of authority that does not hold.

cases.title: Unknown operator
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge's operator is XYZ, which sedi-1 does not know. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it applies a weaker rule than the issuer wrote.

cases.title: Empty operator list
cases.description: As SV-10, but o is the empty list, which reads as absent and so as the default I2I. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Conflicting operators, latest wins
cases.description: F is issued to R, so I2I does not hold, but the edge's operators are [I2I, NI2I] and the latest, NI2I, wins (ACDC line 1186). A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Nested operator list
cases.description: As SV-10, but o is the nested list [[I2I]], which sedi-1 treats as malformed. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it evaluates an instruction the issuer did not write.

cases.title: Edge without its own SAID
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge block carries no d. sedi-1 requires every edge to carry its own SAID. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts an edge that commits to nothing.
